comments.body:
Hmm, I am not seeing the described behavior. When I spin up the one-click, and request:
$curl localhost:8080/rest/fcr:acl

..I get the following response:
```
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix webac: <http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/webac#> .
@prefix acl: <http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#> .
@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .

<http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:acl#authz>
acl:default <http://localhost:8080/rest/> ;
acl:accessTo <http://localhost:8080/rest/> ;
acl:mode acl:Read ;
acl:agentClass <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Agent> ;
rdfs:comment "By default, all non-Admin agents (foaf:Agent) only have read access (acl:Read) to the respository" ;
rdfs:label "Root Authorization" ;
rdf:type acl:Authorization .

<http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:acl>
rdf:type webac:Acl .
```

..or are you describing a different issue?

p.s. Unfortunate about the typo: "respository"

Andrew Woods, that's very odd. I reported this behavior because the root acl does not display in the web console, and it still doesn't. You get: "Error: No OCFL mapping found for info:fedora/fcr:acl"

However, I tried curling for it, as you suggested and got the acl as your described. It seems like there is still a bug here somewhere.
The issue is likely related to: https://jira.lyrasis.org/browse/FCREPO-3423
